newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MIXED OUTLOOK FOR GLOBAL FUNDS - SAFRICA OLD MUTUAL.
newsitem.headline: MIXED OUTLOOK FOR GLOBAL FUNDS - SAFRICA OLD MUTUAL.

text.p: Moderate world economic growth and low inflation pointed to a mixed outlook for international fund managers, South Africa's Old Mutual said on Wednesday.
U.K assets -- gilts, equities and property -- were expected to have a higher return than bank deposits in 1997, said Nigel Morgan an economic strategist at Old Mutual's International Asset Managers.
On a ranking combining risk and reward, however, gilts might be the preferred investment, Morgan said briefing journalists at the launch of the Old Mutual Market Focus 1997.
An international equity portfolio was expected to produce a return that was only a little greater than that available from either a dollar or sterling bank deposit.

In Europe, equity returns were expected to be moderate, supported by lower bond yields. In the U.S., equity returns were expected to be small as share prices were presently high relative to earnings and bond yields.
In Japan, earnings were expected to grow strongly and equities to do well. In Asia, the prospects for equities were poor, with earnings falling heavily as competition intensified.
Morgan said an international bond portfolio was expected to produce a return a little better than that available from either a dollar or a sterling bank deposit.
In Europe, bond yields were expected to fall a little further in response to low inflation as the Maastricht process led to improved public finances.
In the U.S., bond yields were not expected to fall further, even though the economy was slowing.
"A number of fringe markets have better prospects, as do some emerging markets as financial management improves, particularly in Latin America and East Europe," Morgan said.

He said Old Mutual asset managers had started reducing their hedges on the Japanese yen in their global portfolios as that country's growing current account surplus implied a potentially stronger currency.
Old Mutual had hedged its yen positions heavily for the last few years.
